A1.justification: Both 17-page PDFs describe the same VideoGLaMM work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison; the appendices are unchanged.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original grounding and segmentation evaluations, encoder/decoder ablations, and qualitative demonstrations, including additional results in Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains these original empirical evaluations and demonstrations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The dual vision encoders, alignment adapters, LLM, pixel decoder, training objectives and inference procedures in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training sources and task coverage are unchanged, including GCG, VidSTG, MeViS, Ref-DAVIS-17, supplementary Refer-YouTube-VOS evaluation and conditional video-editing demonstrations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and 8, including PG-Video-LLaVA, GLaMM+SAM2, LMPM, LISA, TrackGPT and VideoLISA in their respective comparisons.

E3.justification: Both versions specify the same datasets, evaluation splits, metrics, model configurations, training schedules and frame-count settings. Table 3's reassignment of reported values does not revise the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The encoder, decoder and supervision-frame ablations in Tables 5–7 are retained unchanged, as are the qualitative grounding, segmentation and video-editing examples in Appendix B.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 swaps the J and J&F values for all six Ref-DAVIS-17 rows while retaining F. VideoGLaMM's (J, F, J&F) changes from (69.5, 65.6, 73.3) to (73.3, 65.6, 69.5); VideoLISA's changes from (68.8, 64.9, 72.7) to (72.7, 64.9, 68.8). Rankings remain unchanged. This is a limited metric-assignment correction, not evidence of improved model performance; other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including feature projections, mask prediction and total loss, are unchanged. No formal result, assumption or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about pixel-level video grounding, the curated instruction-tuning dataset and superior performance across three tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of temporal modeling and encoder/decoder tradeoffs are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning annotation noise, incomplete object coverage, object granularity and longer videos.

D1.justification: Model initializations, hardware, training schedules, annotation procedures, Appendix C prompt templates and the project-link disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Differences in reference back-reference page numbers follow text and table relocation.

P1.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 receive small wording trims, and the equal-technical-contribution markers and footnote are removed. Section order and substantive exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 moves from PDF page 8 to page 7 beside Section 5.3, and text reflow brings the complete conclusion onto page 8. Figure content and table structures are retained; appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The Table 3 correction restores consistency with Section 5's definition of J&F as the mean of J and F: VideoGLaMM's revised 69.5 matches the rounded mean of 73.3 and 65.6. This improves reporting accuracy without changing rankings or adding evidence. The remaining edits are limited editorial and layout adjustments.
